title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 102
paragraphs: When Phraortes had brought his life to an end, Cyaxares, son of Phraortes, son of Deioces, received the power. This king is said to have been still much more warlike than his forefathers; and he first banded the men of Asia into separate divisions—that is, he first arrayed apart from one another the spearmen, the archers, and the horsemen, for before that time they had all been mingled together without distinction. This was the man who fought with the Lydians when day became night as they fought, and who also united under his rule the whole of Asia above the river Halys. And having gathered together all his subjects, he marched upon Nineveh to avenge his father, and also because he wished to take the city. After he had fought a battle with the Assyrians and defeated them, while he was sitting in siege before Nineveh, there came upon him a great army of Scythians, whose leader was Madyes, son of Protothyes, king of the Scythians. These had invaded Asia after driving the Cimmerians out of Europe, and in pursuit of them as they fled they had come into the land of Media.
